text: Silence creates rhythm. <break time="0.8s" /> One of the most fundamental aspects of sound. <break time="0.8s" /> For all species. <break time="0.8s" /> Because rhythm implies life, agency, and possibly intention. <break time="0.8s" /> It does this. <break time="0.8s" /> Both by defining the pattern of sounds. <break time="0.8s" /> And by anchoring one end of the continuum of intensity. <break time="0.8s" /> A skilled actor or public speaker. <break time="0.8s" /> Is best friends with silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Using it for emphasis, shock, variation. <break time="0.8s" /> And to amplify meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> One of the commonest failings I see. <break time="0.8s" /> In inexperienced and especially very nervous public speakers. <break time="0.8s" /> Is their fear of silence. <break time="0.8s" /> Which drives them to fill every available moment. <break time="0.8s" /> With gabble or meaningless filler words. <break time="0.8s" /> A top salesperson is as assured and skilled with silence. <break time="0.8s" /> As an expert surgeon with a scalpel. <break time="0.8s" /> Especially when it comes to the close. <break time="0.8s" /> The same goes for elite negotiators. <break time="0.8s" /> Silence is one of the main reasons. <break time="0.8s" /> Speaking is so much more powerful than writing. <break time="0.8s" /> It is very hard to write silences. <break time="0.8s" /> As anyone who has ever given a speech or presentation knows. <break time="0.8s" /> The silence of impressed awe and disengaged boredom. <break time="0.8s" /> May be the same sound. <break time="0.8s" /> But they feel very different. <break time="0.8s" /> Silence is not homogeneous.
